interpretation.plain_speak: A rescue that looks safe for 16–29 unique writes can be forced back into danger after only 8–11 writes if later refreshes protect competing memories. The original horizon is a forecast for one future regime, not a universal guarantee.
interpretation.north_star_question: Separates one-step exact failure prediction from long-run robustness: future workload can reshape how long a correction lasts even when immediate native state is known exactly.
interpretation.next_stage: test a frozen periodic re-check rule that takes no action, asking whether recomputing the native pre-loss warning every few writes can detect the shortened horizon before the rescued item is actually lost
